AbstractText.Label: STUDY OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: The aim of this work was to measure the irisin levels in maternal and umbilical cord serums at cesarean section and vaginal delivery.

AbstractText.Label: STUDY DESIGN
AbstractText.content: This is a case-control study conducted at the Obstetric Department of the Mansoura University Hospital, Mansoura University, Egypt.

AbstractText.Label: MATERIAL AND METHODS
AbstractText.content: The 150 nulliparous cases were divided into three groups.

AbstractText.Label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE
AbstractText.content: Serum irisin concentrations were assayed by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) method.

AbstractText.Label: STATISTICAL ANALYSIS
AbstractText.content: Unpaired t-test and correlation were done by using the Statistical Package for Social Scientists (SPSS).

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The maternal irisin levels in cases with mild preeclampsia were found to be significantly lower than that of the normal cases. In cases with mild preeclampsia, the maternal irisin levels early in labor for vaginal deliveries were significantly higher than that during cesarean section. The maternal irisin levels after vaginal deliveries were significantly higher than the levels early in labor. The maternal serum irisin was a significantly correlated with the duration of the first stage. The umbilical cord serum irisin levels were significantly correlated with the neonatal weight and with the duration of the first stage of labor.

AbstractText.Label: MAJOR CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Labor is a strong stimulus to the release of irisin into the maternal and fetal circulations. Neonatal serum irisin levels are positively correlated with the birth weight and with the duration of the first stage. The neonatal birth weight and the duration of the first stage of labor are positively correlated with the umbilical cord serum irisin levels.
